learning: If oval oscillation falls below 0.25 with the score at or above 215, yaw gain drives the oscillation and kp/wheel_track near 35 is the working point. If the score falls, the controller at kp 3.2 is the suspect, and kp 3.5 with kd 0.45 is the fallback.
notes: Complete robot for the held iteration 8 geometry with kp 3.2 and kd 0.5. The only change is the kp step taken to bring oval oscillation down, based on iteration 5's yaw-gain link and iteration 7's oscillation of 0.291.
rationale: Iteration 9 holds the iteration 8 geometry exactly (wheel_track 0.09 m, five 12 mm sensors at x = -0.024 to +0.024 m, y = 0.04 m, mass 0.6 kg). The controller is the one that scored 215.38 in iteration 8: kp 3.2, ki 0.2, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.8, sensor_weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2], line_loss last_direction. Iteration 7 (kp 3.5, kd 0.5) scored 213.28 with oval steering_oscillation 0.291. Iteration 6 (kp 3.5, kd 0.3) scored 153 with oscillation 0.2505. Lowering kp to 3.2 reduces yaw gain (kp/wheel_track falls from 38.9 to 35.6) and is the only change from iteration 7, so the race isolates the controller. I considered lowering kd back toward 0.3, but kd 0.5 is what lifted the score from 153 to 213, so I keep it. Expected result: oval steering_oscillation below about 0.25 and a score at or above 215. Because the geometry is held, a score drop points to the controller. Observation requests are kept broad so the oval oscillation, s-bend max_error and line-loss counts can be read per track.
